audit_status.review_note: Reviewed as Job's opening lament: curse of birth-day, night of conception, Leviathan imagery, death/rest language, and anguished why-questions. Poetic lines are compact but verse-complete.

verses.restored: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed his day.

familiar.text: After this opened Job his mouth, and cursed his day.

modern.text: After this, Job opened his mouth and cursed the day of his birth.

original.text: אַחֲרֵי כֵ֗ן פָּתַ֤ח אִיּוֹב֙ אֶת פִּ֔יהוּ וַיְקַלֵּ֖ל אֶת יוֹמֽוֹ

verses.restored: Job answered and said:

familiar.text: And Job spake, and said,

modern.text: And this is what he said:

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר

verses.restored: Let the day perish on which I was born, and the night that said, A male has been conceived.

familiar.text: Let the day perish wherein I was born, and the night in which it was said, There is a man child conceived.

modern.text: “May the day of my birth perish, and the night it was said, ‘A boy is conceived.’

original.text: יֹ֣אבַד י֭וֹם אִוָּ֣לֶד בּ֑וֹ וְהַלַּ֥יְלָה אָ֝מַ֗ר הֹ֣רָה גָֽבֶר

verses.restored: Let that day be darkness. Let the Divine above not seek it, and let no light shine upon it.

familiar.text: Let that day be darkness; let not God regard it from above, neither let the light shine upon it.

modern.text: If only that day had turned to darkness! May God above disregard it; may no light shine upon it.

original.text: הַיּ֥וֹם הַה֗וּא יְֽהִ֫י חֹ֥שֶׁךְ אַֽל יִדְרְשֵׁ֣הוּ אֱל֣וֹהַּ מִמָּ֑עַל וְאַל תּוֹפַ֖ע עָלָ֣יו נְהָרָֽה

verses.restored: Let darkness and deep shadow reclaim it. Let a cloud dwell upon it. Let the blackness of day terrify it.

familiar.text: Let darkness and the shadow of death stain it; let a cloud dwell upon it; let the blackness of the day terrify it.

modern.text: May darkness and gloom reclaim it, and a cloud settle over it; may the blackness of the day overwhelm it.

original.text: יִגְאָלֻ֡הוּ חֹ֣שֶׁךְ וְ֭צַלְמָוֶת תִּשְׁכָּן עָלָ֣יו עֲנָנָ֑ה יְ֝בַעֲתֻ֗הוּ כִּֽמְרִ֥ירֵי יֽוֹם

verses.restored: That night, let thick darkness take it. Let it not rejoice among the days of the year; let it not come into the number of months.

familiar.text: As for that night, let darkness seize upon it; let it not be joined unto the days of the year, let it not come into the number of the months.

modern.text: If only darkness had taken that night away! May it not appear among the days of the year; may it never be entered in any of the months.

original.text: הַלַּ֥יְלָה הַהוּא֮ יִקָּחֵ֪ה֫וּ אֹ֥פֶל אַל יִ֭חַדְּ בִּימֵ֣י שָׁנָ֑ה בְּמִסְפַּ֥ר יְ֝רָחִ֗ים אַל יָבֹֽא

verses.restored: Look, let that night be barren; let no joyful cry enter it.

familiar.text: Lo, let that night be solitary, let no joyful voice come therein.

modern.text: Behold, may that night be barren; may no joyful voice come into it.

original.text: הִנֵּ֤ה הַלַּ֣יְלָה הַ֭הוּא יְהִ֣י גַלְמ֑וּד אַל תָּבֹ֖א רְנָנָ֣ה בֽוֹ

verses.restored: Let those who curse the day curse it, those ready to rouse Leviathan.

familiar.text: Let them curse it that curse the day, who are ready to raise up their mourning.

modern.text: May it be cursed by those who curse the day — those prepared to rouse Leviathan.

original.text: יִקְּבֻ֥הוּ אֹרְרֵי י֑וֹם הָ֝עֲתִידִ֗ים עֹרֵ֥ר לִוְיָתָֽן

verses.restored: Let the stars of its dawn be dark. Let it wait for light and have none, and let it not see the eyelids of morning.

familiar.text: Let the stars of the twilight thereof be dark; let it look for light, but have none; neither let it see the dawning of the day:

modern.text: May its morning stars grow dark; may it wait in vain for daylight; may it not see the breaking of dawn.

original.text: יֶחְשְׁכוּ֮ כּוֹכְבֵ֪י נִ֫שְׁפּ֥וֹ יְקַו לְא֥וֹר וָאַ֑יִן וְאַל יִ֝רְאֶ֗ה בְּעַפְעַפֵּי שָֽׁחַר

verses.restored: Because it did not shut the doors of my mother’s womb, nor hide trouble from my eyes.

familiar.text: Because it shut not up the doors of my mother’s womb, nor hid sorrow from mine eyes.

modern.text: For that night did not shut the doors of the womb to hide the sorrow from my eyes.

original.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א סָ֭גַר דַּלְתֵ֣י בִטְנִ֑י וַיַּסְתֵּ֥ר עָ֝מָ֗ל מֵעֵינָֽי

verses.restored: Why did I not die from the womb, come out from the belly and expire?

familiar.text: Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?

modern.text: Why did I not perish at birth; why did I not die as I came from the womb?

original.text: לָ֤מָּה לֹּ֣א מֵרֶ֣חֶם אָמ֑וּת מִבֶּ֖טֶן יָצָ֣אתִי וְאֶגְוָֽע

verses.restored: Why did knees receive me, and why breasts, that I should nurse?

familiar.text: Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?

modern.text: Why were there knees to receive me, and breasts that I should be nursed?

original.text: מַ֭דּוּעַ קִדְּמ֣וּנִי בִרְכָּ֑יִם וּמַה שָּׁ֝דַ֗יִם כִּ֣י אִינָֽק

verses.restored: For now I would have lain down and been quiet; I would have slept; then I would be at rest,

familiar.text: For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest,

modern.text: For now I would be lying down in peace; I would be asleep and at rest

original.text: כִּֽי עַ֭תָּה שָׁכַ֣בְתִּי וְאֶשְׁק֑וֹט יָ֝שַׁ֗נְתִּי אָ֤ז יָנ֬וּחַֽ לִֽי

verses.restored: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built ruins for themselves,

familiar.text: With kings and counsellors of the earth, which built desolate places for themselves;

modern.text: with kings and counselors of the earth, who built for themselves cities now in ruins,

original.text: עִם מְ֭לָכִים וְיֹ֣עֲצֵי אָ֑רֶץ הַבֹּנִ֖ים חֳרָב֣וֹת לָֽמוֹ

verses.restored: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.

familiar.text: Or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver:

modern.text: or with princes who had gold, who filled their houses with silver.

original.text: א֣וֹ עִם שָׂ֭רִים זָהָ֣ב לָהֶ֑ם הַֽמְמַלְאִ֖ים בָּתֵּיהֶ֣ם כָּֽסֶף

verses.restored: Or why was I not like a hidden miscarriage, like infants who never saw light?

familiar.text: Or as an hidden untimely birth I had not been; as infants which never saw light.

modern.text: Or why was I not hidden like a stillborn child, like an infant who never sees daylight?

original.text: א֤וֹ כְנֵ֣פֶל טָ֭מוּן לֹ֣א אֶהְיֶ֑ה כְּ֝עֹלְלִ֗ים לֹא רָ֥אוּ אֽוֹר

verses.restored: There the wicked cease from agitation, and there the weary of strength rest.

familiar.text: There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest.

modern.text: There the wicked cease from raging, and there the weary find rest.

original.text: שָׁ֣ם רְ֭שָׁעִים חָ֣דְלוּ רֹ֑גֶז וְשָׁ֥ם יָ֝נ֗וּחוּ יְגִ֣יעֵי כֹֽחַ

verses.restored: Captives are at ease together; they do not hear the voice of the taskmaster.

familiar.text: There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.

modern.text: The captives enjoy their ease; they do not hear the voice of the oppressor.

original.text: יַ֭חַד אֲסִירִ֣ים שַׁאֲנָ֑נוּ לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ ק֣וֹל נֹגֵֽשׂ

verses.restored: Small and great are there, and the servant is free from his master.

familiar.text: The small and great are there; and the servant is free from his master.

modern.text: Both small and great are there, and the slave is freed from his master.

original.text: קָטֹ֣ן וְ֭גָדוֹל שָׁ֣ם ה֑וּא וְ֝עֶ֗בֶד חָפְשִׁ֥י מֵאֲדֹנָֽיו

verses.restored: Why does he give light to the troubled, and life to the bitter of soul,

familiar.text: Wherefore is light given to him that is in misery, and life unto the bitter in soul;

modern.text: Why is light given to the miserable, and life to the bitter of soul,

original.text: לָ֤מָּה יִתֵּ֣ן לְעָמֵ֣ל א֑וֹר וְ֝חַיִּ֗ים לְמָ֣רֵי נָֽפֶשׁ

verses.restored: who wait for death, but it is not there, and dig for it more than hidden treasures,

familiar.text: Which long for death, but it cometh not; and dig for it more than for hid treasures;

modern.text: who long for death that does not come, and search for it like hidden treasure,

original.text: הַֽמְחַכִּ֣ים לַמָּ֣וֶת וְאֵינֶ֑נּוּ וַֽ֝יַּחְפְּרֻ֗הוּ מִמַּטְמוֹנִֽים

verses.restored: who rejoice greatly and are glad when they find the grave?

familiar.text: Which rejoice exceedingly, and are glad, when they can find the grave?

modern.text: who rejoice and greatly exult when they can find the grave?

original.text: הַשְּׂמֵחִ֥ים אֱלֵי גִ֑יל יָ֝שִׂ֗ישׂוּ כִּ֣י יִמְצְאוּ קָֽבֶר

verses.restored: Why give light to a man whose way is hidden, whom the Divine has hedged in?

familiar.text: Why is light given to a man whose way is hid, and whom God hath hedged in?

modern.text: Why is life given to a man whose way is hidden, whom God has hedged in?

original.text: לְ֭גֶבֶר אֲשֶׁר דַּרְכּ֣וֹ נִסְתָּ֑רָה וַיָּ֖סֶךְ אֱל֣וֹהַּ בַּעֲדֽוֹ

verses.restored: For my sighing comes before my bread, and my groanings pour out like waters.

familiar.text: For my sighing cometh before I eat, and my roarings are poured out like the waters.

modern.text: I sigh when food is put before me, and my groans pour out like water.

original.text: כִּֽי לִפְנֵ֣י לַ֭חְמִי אַנְחָתִ֣י תָבֹ֑א וַֽיִּתְּכ֥וּ כַ֝מַּ֗יִם שַׁאֲגֹתָֽי

verses.restored: For the dread I dreaded has come upon me, and what I feared has arrived at me.

familiar.text: For the thing which I greatly feared is come upon me, and that which I was afraid of is come unto me.

modern.text: For the thing I feared has overtaken me, and what I dreaded has befallen me.

original.text: כִּ֤י פַ֣חַד פָּ֭חַדְתִּי וַיֶּאֱתָיֵ֑נִי וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יָ֝גֹ֗רְתִּי יָ֣בֹא לִֽי

verses.restored: I was not at ease, I was not quiet, I did not rest, and turmoil came.

familiar.text: I was not in safety, neither had I rest, neither was I quiet; yet trouble came.

modern.text: I am not at ease or quiet; I have no rest, for trouble has come.”

original.text: לֹ֤א שָׁלַ֨וְתִּי וְלֹ֖א שָׁקַ֥טְתִּי וְֽלֹא נָ֗חְתִּי וַיָּ֥בֹא רֹֽגֶז
